title: Exceptional preservation for all-continuous algebraic-closure coefficients
statement: Fix a prime ell and a field k of positive prime characteristic p different from ell. Let X,Y be separated finite-type k-schemes and f:X -> Y a separated finite-type k-morphism [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let Lambda be a commutative condensed ring isomorphic, as a ring object, to S |-> C(S,Qbar_ell), with ALL continuous maps for the induced ell-adic topology [sk-def-localizing-closure]. In the ordinary unbounded derived categories with the pulled-back coefficients, let Loc(Dctf) be the localizing closures [sk-def-localizing-closure] of the bounded constructible finite-Tor objects [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Fix a boundary compactification c of f and a proof h that its actual compactification lower shriek preserves those closures. For any right adjoint G to that restricted lower shriek and any supplied adjunction [sk-prop-sf-existence], G sends Dctf(Y,Lambda) into Dctf(X,Lambda). This assertion only states preservation, without constructing functor restrictions or a restricted adjunction.

proof.text: Keep the finite-subextension-valued coefficient C and the all-continuous coefficient B distinct. On each finite-type k-scheme the topology scalar functor J restricts to an equivalence of bounded constructible categories. Both constructible properties equal their intersections with finite Tor amplitude: use the rational equality for C and continuous-algebraic-closure constructible Tor for B. Finite type over k supplies Noetherianity.

source.place: First two proof paragraphs and restricted-adjunction argument, transported by the constructible coefficient-topology equivalence.

proof.text: Define the natural proper-pushforward comparison as the geometric adjunction mate of the specified topology pullback comparison. Its component equals algClTopologyCounitMate. Proper finiteness puts both endpoints in the B-constructible category. The mate Hom-bijection, extended to all B-constructible tests by essential surjectivity of J, makes postcomposition bijective. Testing with its two endpoints constructs a two-sided inverse.

source.place: First two proof paragraphs and restricted-adjunction argument, transported by the constructible coefficient-topology equivalence.

proof.text: For the supplied boundary compactification combine this proper comparison with the derived open-extension coefficient isomorphism. Open lower shriek preserves the C-constructible finite-Tor property. Thus the resulting natural transformation is invertible at every constructible object and identifies the actual two restricted compactification composites.

proof.text: Choose the rational C-localizing right adjoint using existence and apply rationalRestrictionGlue to obtain its constructible adjunction. This retains the unit sk-thm-restriction affine-space purity, closed-support, and finite-cover route through that existing theorem. Conjugate the constructible adjunction by the two scalar equivalences and the actual compactification comparison. For B, compactification_localizing and constructible Tor make the left functor the actual B-restricted compactification functor.

source.place: First two proof paragraphs and restricted-adjunction argument, transported by the constructible coefficient-topology equivalence.

proof.text: Compare the transported constructible right adjoint with the supplied localizing right adjoint using the proved generic rightAdjoint_preserves_generators helper of EtaleProEtaleAdjunctionTransfer. Its small counit transposes under the large adjunction; postcomposition is bijective on Hom from every shifted constructible generator, so the comparison is an isomorphism by the localizing cone test. This proves bounded constructibility, and the B Tor theorem supplies finite Tor amplitude. Finally transport the supplied adjunction along the stated coefficient-ring isomorphism. The exact coefficient equivalences preserve the actual ambient-intersection localizing closures and reflect bounded constructible finite-Tor objects.
